## Batch 1 scaffold complete — `handle-decompositions-duality-and-rearrangement`

**Deliverables** (all in the run namespace, no published/shared files touched):

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `research/frontier-41-ha-dt-29-batch-1.pages.json` | 29 A items (16 designed + 13 local prerequisites) and 5 B items, each with `id/kind/title/deps/statement/strategy/provenance/sources/dependency_level/justified_by` |

**Mathematics.** The A page builds the compact-cobordism language, adapted Morse functions/fields (library descending convention), the Morse↔handle correspondence, the relative-CW homotopy model, duality via $1-f$, and rearrangement in the Milnor/Pajitnov form: the interchange lemma for disjoint trajectory closures, the Sard-based separation of adjacent levels when the lower index is at least the upper, bubble-sort rearrangement by index, self-indexing (one level per index), equal-index grouping, and elimination of $0$-/$n$-handles. New local lemmas close the real gaps I found: the interior-slab form of DT-5 attachment, the standard handle Morse model and its collar gluing, the handle-to-cell homotopy step, boundary-sum absorption of a $0$-handle, level-sphere product neighbourhoods, moving a sphere off a lower-dimensional submanifold, flow realization of level isotopies, and endpoint-fixing increasing reparametrisation.

**Recorded conflicts (plan controls).** (1) Design says "Requires DT-2–DT-5" but the plan's exact `requires` omits DT-4; the scaffold needs no Morse–Smale and avoids DT-4's items, which reach the published global stable/unstable theorem flagged as asserted-not-proved in design §12.7(3) — recorded for the canonical ledger. (2) The classical "gradient inward at $M_0$" clause was translated to the library's descending convention (outward at $M_0$, inward at $M_1$). (3) Pajitnov's rearrangement material is Ch. 4 §3, not the design's Ch. 5 locator. (4) The connecting-trajectory counterexample is stated precisely for a fixed field; the full rearrangement can first separate the pair.

**Checks (final snapshot):** coverage-checklist `--require-destination` 0 errors; source-fetch-check 3/3 stamped and resolved; url-sweep 3/3 live; manifest-deps whole run 148 items, 0 errors; content-policy `--manifest-only` whole run 0 errors; validate-plan, extcheck, drift-review-check pass; item-dependency-levels check has no batch-1 finding (max level 8, 78 in-run edges); all 34 batch-1 readiness records current. `frontier-dependency-ledger --require-reviewed` remains red only because the five consumer batches (3, 4, 13, 15, 17) have yet to record their reviews — operator/engine reconciliation, not a batch-1 blocker. Step-3 authoring review and the full engine gate remain.
